## Lib/eacp/Network/IPC/Messenger.h

- class `Messenger` — eacp::IPC — Messenger.h:23 — One live conversation with another of this user's processes, ready for app code: where a Channel is a byte stream and a manual reader thread, a Messenger is whole messages and main-thread callbacks.
  - ctor `Messenger(std::string_view name, Time::MS timeout)` — :29 — Dials the server named name in the background, retrying until timeout elapses. onConnected fires when the peer answers; onDisconnected fires instead when nobody did.
  - dtor `~Messenger()` — :33 — Interrupts the reader, joins it and closes the channel.
  - method `bool isConnected() const` — :40
  - method `void send(const std::string& message)` — :48 — Hands message to the peer, whole: it arrives as one onMessage there, however large.
  - field `Callback onConnected` — :52 — The dial landed (dialing Messengers only: a server-side session arrives in onClient already connected, and this never fires there).
  - field `std::function<void (std::string)> onMessage` — :56 — A whole message from the peer, handed over by value: a receiver that wants to keep the bytes moves them out instead of copying.
  - field `Callback onDisconnected` — :60 — The conversation is over and cannot resume: the peer left, the stream broke, or the dial never landed.
- class `MessageServer` — eacp::IPC — Messenger.h:86 — The serving end: claims a name and turns every client that dials in into a live Messenger session.
  - ctor `MessageServer(std::string_view name)` — :92 — Claims name and starts accepting, or throws IPC::Error - most notably when another live server already holds the name (the ChannelServer rules apply).
  - dtor `~MessageServer()` — :94
  - field `std::function<void (Messenger&)> onClient` — :104 — A client dialed in. The session is already connected - wire its onMessage / onDisconnected here; nothing it received can be delivered before this handler returns.
